item.title: Milton residents alarmed over injured alligator with taped mouth, hook in snout
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A well-known alligator living near Mulatto Bayou in Milton has become the focus of concern after residents spotted it with its mouth taped shut and a hook lodged in its snout, according to WKRG News 5. The injured reptile has been a familiar presence in the Santa Rosa County community, and neighbors say they're worried about its welfare and what…
item.content:encoded:
A well-known alligator living near Mulatto Bayou in Milton has become the focus of concern after residents spotted it with its mouth taped shut and a hook lodged in its snout, according to WKRG News 5.

The injured reptile has been a familiar presence in the Santa Rosa County community, and neighbors say they're worried about its welfare and what may have caused the injuries. The discovery has sparked alarm among locals who have grown accustomed to seeing the animal in the area.

It's unclear how the alligator sustained the injuries or whether anyone has reported the incident to wildlife authorities. Residents are hoping the animal receives help to remove the tape and hook before its condition worsens.

item.content:encoded: Thomas Hospital in Fairhope, Alabama has opened a new emergency helipad, giving medical helicopters direct access to the facility and cutting response times for critically ill or injured patients across the region. According to WKRG News 5, the addition addresses a key gap in trauma care infrastructure—in emergencies, minutes can mean the difference between life and death, and the helipad eliminates delays from ground transport. The new facility is now operational and available for incoming patients requiring rapid air evacuation or transfer to the hospital's emergency department.

The Escambia County Sheriff's Office got into the Halloween spirit this week with an employee pumpkin decorating contest that ended in a three-way tie for top honors.

Details about the winning designs and how the tie was decided were not immediately available.

item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced today the reappointment of MaryLynn Magar to the State Board of Education, pending Florida Senate confirmation.

Magar, currently Vice President at Heartcare Imaging, Inc., previously served in the Florida House of Representatives from 2012 to 2020, including a stint as Speaker pro tempore from 2018 to 2020. She hails from Martin County in South Florida and has been active in local civic organizations, including the Hobe Sound Chamber of Commerce and Northern Palm Beach Chamber of Commerce. She also served as a trustee for All Saints Catholic School.

The appointment requires approval from the state Senate before it becomes final.

item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced Friday the appointment of Andrew Dulcey, a Key West attorney, to the Florida Keys Aqueduct Authority.

Dulcey currently serves as a board member of the College of the Florida Keys District Board of Trustees and holds membership in the Key West Maritime Historical Society and the Key West International Airport Ad-Hoc Committee on Noise. He earned his juris doctor from the University of Miami.

The Florida Keys Aqueduct Authority oversees water supply infrastructure serving the Keys region. The appointment comes as part of the governor's ongoing efforts to fill positions on state boards and authorities across Florida.

item.title: DeSantis Reappoints Four to State Board of Pharmacy, Including Escambia Pharmacist
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced today the reappointment of four members to Florida's Board of Pharmacy, including Darrell Miller, a consultant pharmacist with Escambia County ties. Miller, who previously served as president of the Escambia County Pharmacy Association and held leadership roles at Community Health Northwest Florida and other…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced today the reappointment of four members to Florida's Board of Pharmacy, including Darrell Miller, a consultant pharmacist with Escambia County ties. Miller, who previously served as president of the Escambia County Pharmacy Association and held leadership roles at Community Health Northwest Florida and other regional healthcare organizations, earned his pharmacy degrees from Auburn University and the University of Florida.

The other three reappointees are Leigh Mathes, director of operations for Coastal Med of Florida; Cristina Medina, a pharmacist with CVS Health; and Dorinda Segovia, vice president and chief pharmacy officer for Memorial Healthcare System. All four bring extensive professional credentials and involvement with state and national pharmacy associations.

The appointments require confirmation by the Florida Senate. The Board of Pharmacy oversees licensing, regulation, and discipline of pharmacists and pharmacy operations throughout the state.

item.title: DeSantis Appoints Seven to Florida Board of Medicine; One Has Pensacola Ties
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced appointments and reappointments to the Florida Board of Medicine on Friday, including Dr. Matthew Benson, who earned his undergraduate degree from Pensacola Christian College. Among the appointees is Dr. Andrea Aguilera, a pediatrician with the Emergency Resources Group who previously worked for Nicklaus Children's…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced appointments and reappointments to the Florida Board of Medicine on Friday, including Dr. Matthew Benson, who earned his undergraduate degree from Pensacola Christian College.

Among the appointees is Dr. Andrea Aguilera, a pediatrician with the Emergency Resources Group who previously worked for Nicklaus Children's Health System. Also appointed are Elyse Young, who brings 20 years of state government experience in budgeting and healthcare policy.

Reappointed to the board are Dr. Scot Ackerman, Medical Director of the Ackerman Cancer Center in Jacksonville; Dr. Gobi Balaji, founder and CEO of Brevard Health Center; Dr. Benson, a pediatric endocrinologist at Nemours Children's Health; Dr. Lisa Kay Mao, a clinical ophthalmologist with over 30 years in Florida; and Dr. Hector Vila, an anesthesiologist and owner of Pediatric Dental Anesthesia Associates.

The Board of Medicine regulates physician licensing, discipline, and practice standards across Florida.

item.title: Santa Rosa County November Events: Markets, Music, Racing & More
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County is packed with entertainment and community activities this November, according to a roundup from Santa Rosa County Communications & Media Relations. For farmers market fans, the Navarre Farmers' Market runs every Saturday from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Combs of Honey (Highway 87 & Segura Corner, across from Tractor Supply). You'll find…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is packed with entertainment and community activities this November, according to a roundup from Santa Rosa County Communications & Media Relations.

For farmers market fans, the Navarre Farmers' Market runs every Saturday from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Combs of Honey (Highway 87 & Segura Corner, across from Tractor Supply). You'll find fresh local produce, dairy, baked goods including gluten-free options, handcrafted soaps and candles, and live plants. The Highway 87 Outdoor Market at Pik-itz also opens Saturdays, 9 a.m.–2 p.m., featuring farm-to-table vendors and arts & crafts.

Music and entertainment venues are active throughout the month. Juana's Pagodas hosts live music Friday and Saturday nights from 8 p.m. to midnight at Navarre Beach (free admission), while Andy D's on Navarre Beach features live music from local and regional acts on varying nights. Stripes Pub & Grill in Navarre has UFC fights, comedy shows, and live music scheduled, and Beardless Brewhaus in downtown Milton hosts Bingo Night every Wednesday at 6:30 p.m.

For outdoor enthusiasts, Holley Hill Pottery in Navarre opens Tuesday through Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., where visitors can watch potters fire the kiln and browse the gallery. Hunt the Front Southern Speedway in Milton offers dirt track racing most Saturdays, and the Navarre Beach Sea Turtle Rescue Team holds Turtle Chat sessions on Tuesday mornings in November at 10 a.m. at Andy D's.

item.content:encoded:
A chance of showers and thunderstorms is expected across the Pensacola area this Halloween weekend as clouds continue to stream into Northwest Florida, according to WKRG News 5.

Cloudy conditions have already moved into the region Friday, creating the atmospheric setup for wet weather Saturday and Sunday. Residents planning Halloween activities should keep an eye on the forecast and have backup indoor plans ready.

Looking further ahead, forecasters are also monitoring a potential round of severe weather next week that could impact the area.

item.title: Federal Indictment: Mobile Tax Scheme Sought $177 Million, IRS Paid About $81 Million
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: MOBILE, AL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Federal prosecutors say an alleged tax-fraud operation in Mobile filed more than 9,000 fraudulent returns seeking more than $177 million from the federal government — and approximately $81 million was actually paid out . Six defendants have been indicted in federal court. The U.S. Attorney's Office says Jennifer…
item.content:encoded:
MOBILE, AL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Federal prosecutors say an alleged tax-fraud operation in Mobile filed more than 9,000 fraudulent returns seeking more than $177 million from the federal government — and approximately $81 million was actually paid out.

Six defendants have been indicted in federal court.

The U.S. Attorney's Office says Jennifer Beverly, 47, owned and operated JB Accounting Tax Service in Mobile from approximately 2022 through 2024.

Beverly and five other defendants are accused of participating in a scheme to prepare and submit false federal tax returns between approximately 2021 and 2024.

Prosecutors say the returns contained allegedly fraudulent items including business deductions, COVID-19 credits, fuel-tax credits, estimated tax payments and education credits.

Altogether, the indictment alleges more than 9,000 fraudulent returns sought over $177 million in refunds.

The IRS issued approximately $81 million.

All six defendants are charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud.

Beverly also faces 63 individual wire-fraud counts, while the other defendants face varying numbers of additional wire-fraud charges.

Federal prosecutors are also seeking forfeiture of alleged proceeds from the scheme. The indictment identifies 12 properties belonging to one or more defendants as potentially subject to forfeiture.

The investigation involves IRS Criminal Investigation and the FBI.

An indictment contains allegations. All six defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

item.title: FEMA Individual Assistance Applications Open for Escambia, Santa Rosa Hurricane Victims
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia and Santa Rosa County residents with damage or losses from Hurricane Isaias can now apply directly for federal disaster assistance. President Donald Trump amended Florida's Major Disaster Declaration Thursday to approve FEMA Individual Assistance in eight Panhandle counties. Along with Escambia and Santa…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia and Santa Rosa County residents with damage or losses from Hurricane Isaias can now apply directly for federal disaster assistance.

President Donald Trump amended Florida's Major Disaster Declaration Thursday to approve FEMA Individual Assistance in eight Panhandle counties.

Along with Escambia and Santa Rosa, the declaration covers Bay, Gulf, Holmes, Okaloosa, Walton and Washington counties.

Individual Assistance can provide qualifying residents with grants for temporary housing and essential home repairs along with assistance for serious storm-related needs and uninsured losses.

Residents should file insurance claims as soon as possible, but do not have to wait for an insurance settlement before applying to FEMA.

Applicants should be prepared to provide information including their Social Security number, address of the storm-damaged property, insurance information, household contact information and a description of their losses.

When applying online, residents should select Florida, choose Hurricane Isaias and enter the ZIP code for the damaged property.

Federal Public Assistance had already been approved earlier this week for Escambia and Santa Rosa counties and other affected areas. That program reimburses eligible government recovery costs.

The Individual Assistance approval announced Thursday extends federal recovery assistance directly to qualifying homeowners and renters.

Residents can apply online, through the FEMA mobile app or by calling 800-621-3362.

item.title: Florida's first flying car demo takes off in Tampa Bay today
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis was in Tampa Bay this morning to highlight Florida's role in advanced air mobility as electric aircraft took to the skies for the state's first official demonstration flight. The event recreated the historic 1914 commercial airline route between St. Petersburg and Tampa—over a century later, this time with vertical…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis was in Tampa Bay this morning to highlight Florida's role in advanced air mobility as electric aircraft took to the skies for the state's first official demonstration flight. The event recreated the historic 1914 commercial airline route between St. Petersburg and Tampa—over a century later, this time with vertical takeoff-and-landing aircraft.

The demonstration is part of the FAA's eVTOL and Advanced Air Mobility Integration Pilot Program, which is testing whether electric "flying cars" can become a practical part of Florida's transportation network. Companies including Joby Aviation and BETA Technologies are involved in the effort, which the state says could eventually move people and goods over some of Florida's most congested highways.

According to the Governor's Press Office, BETA Technologies has already run nine flights a day along the I-4 corridor earlier this year, with energy costs below $17 per leg. Florida Department of Transportation Secretary Jared Perdue called today's flights "an important step forward" in what he described as taking "highways to the sky." The state is planning additional demonstrations across central Florida and the Space Coast as part of its "Future of Flight Series."

item.title: Florida Education Data Breach Could Affect 4.9 Million People, Expose Social Security Numbers
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: TALLAHASSEE, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Nearly five million people may have had sensitive personal information exposed in a data breach involving Florida's student financial aid system. The Florida Department of Education announced Thursday that criminals gained unauthorized access to department information through the Florida Student Financial Aid…
item.content:encoded:
TALLAHASSEE, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Nearly five million people may have had sensitive personal information exposed in a data breach involving Florida's student financial aid system.

The Florida Department of Education announced Thursday that criminals gained unauthorized access to department information through the Florida Student Financial Aid website.

The department says approximately 4.9 million people may be affected, and compromised information includes Social Security numbers.

The breach was discovered Oct. 19.

FDOE says the incident currently appears limited to the financial aid website. The department activated its cybersecurity response, contained the unauthorized activity and is working with the Florida Department of Law Enforcement and Florida Digital Service on the investigation.

Officials have not publicly identified who was responsible or explained how the system was accessed.

The department says current financial aid is not at risk.

The breach is not expected to affect eligibility for state scholarships, grants or student loans, and officials say financial aid disbursements and tuition payments will continue.

People who have used Florida's student financial aid system are being encouraged to monitor bank and online accounts, check credit reports for unfamiliar activity and consider placing a fraud alert or credit freeze.

FDOE says some online services may experience disruptions while the cybersecurity response continues.

item.title: Sen. Rick Scott Unveils Plan to Address Rising College Costs
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott released a new video today outlining his approach to tackling skyrocketing higher education costs, which he says have surged roughly 1,570% over the past 50 years and left students buried in debt. Scott, a Florida Republican, argues that federal student lending has incentivized universities to raise tuition while outcomes…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott released a new video today outlining his approach to tackling skyrocketing higher education costs, which he says have surged roughly 1,570% over the past 50 years and left students buried in debt.

Scott, a Florida Republican, argues that federal student lending has incentivized universities to raise tuition while outcomes for graduates have worsened. "When the federal government started lending unlimited amounts of money to kids for a college education, universities took advantage, tuition costs skyrocketed, and outcomes for students got worse," Scott said in a statement. He's calling for smaller government, university accountability, and a return to affordable, effective education.

As Florida governor, Scott championed affordability measures including a $10,000 degree challenge and froze tuition increases at public colleges and universities between 2012 and 2018. By the end of his tenure, every Florida public college and university offering bachelor's degrees offered at least one program at the $10,000 price point. Scott's latest education proposal is part of his broader "Rescuing America" project, which focuses on balancing the federal budget, cutting regulations, and spurring private-sector job growth.

item.content:encoded:
A temporary flight restriction has been issued for Pensacola from November 5 through November 7, signaling the return of the Blue Angels air show to the area, according to FAA notices posted Thursday.

The restriction, issued via NOTAM 6/4028, covers the three-day period and is typical for air shows and sporting events held in the region. The Blue Angels, the U.S. Navy's elite flight demonstration squadron based at NAS Pensacola, regularly draws large crowds to the area during their performances.

Listeners should expect increased air traffic in the area during the weekend and plan accordingly if traveling near the air show venue.

item.title: Northwest Florida Wins Disaster Declaration; Individual Aid Still Uncertain
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Northwest Florida has received an official disaster declaration, a critical step toward securing federal recovery resources following what appears to be a significant weather event. However, according to reporting from WPMI NBC 15, the declaration does not automatically unlock individual assistance for residents and businesses affected by the…
item.content:encoded:
Northwest Florida has received an official disaster declaration, a critical step toward securing federal recovery resources following what appears to be a significant weather event. However, according to reporting from WPMI NBC 15, the declaration does not automatically unlock individual assistance for residents and businesses affected by the disaster.

The distinction is important for the Pensacola area and surrounding counties. A disaster declaration typically allows state and federal agencies to mobilize emergency response, deploy resources, and begin debris removal and emergency protective measures. Individual assistance—direct financial aid to residents for uninsured or underinsured losses—requires a separate approval process and depends on damage assessments and eligibility determinations.

Residents waiting for individual assistance payments will need to register with FEMA and document their losses. The process can take weeks or longer, depending on the scope of damage and the number of applications received. Officials continue to review damage reports across the region to determine whether individual assistance will be warranted.
